name: Federal Customs Service of the Russian Federation

summary.text: Russia's Federal Customs Service is the customs agency of the Russian government. In May 2007 it sued the Bank of New York in Moscow for $22.5 billion, invoking the treble-damages provision of the U.S. RICO statute over the movement of Russian money through the bank's Benex and BECS accounts in the 1990s. Proceedings in the Moscow court resumed in July 2008; in 2009 Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin said the matter would be settled with the bank paying at least $14 million in court costs.

facts.claim: The Federal Customs Service sought $22.5 billion from the Bank of New York beginning in May 2007, claiming the bank helped move $7.5 billion out of Russia in the 1990s and suing for triple that amount under the U.S. Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act.
facts.quote: It sued for triple that amount under the U.S. Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act, or RICO

facts.claim: The suit was filed in Moscow rather than in a U.S. federal court; commentators described the attempt to argue RICO in a foreign court as unprecedented.

facts.claim: The Russian claim rested on the bank's 2005 U.S. resolution; Fortune reported in October 2008 that U.S. prosecutors stated the bank had not admitted criminal culpability with respect to the Southern District investigation of the Russian accounts.
facts.quote: the Bank did not admit criminal culpability with respect to the subject of the SDNY USAO investigation

facts.claim: The Moscow Times reported that Bank of New York Mellon would pay at least $14 million in court costs to settle the Customs Service suit, according to Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin, and that the bank, which had called the suit without merit, said it would not pay more than that.
facts.quote: Bank of New York Mellon would pay at least $14 million in court costs to settle the lawsuit, Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin said

openQuestions: The Moscow Times settlement article's date is not shown in the search listing; the 2009 date rests on the French-language report of 22 October 2009 and on Kudrin's remarks.
The Moscow Times also reported that Russia would receive a loan from the bank which Kudrin called an 'act of goodwill' unrelated to the settlement; the terms were not found.

The site does not name the Customs Service directly; its BoNY entry describes a capital-flight mechanism. The Customs Service suit alleged $7.5 billion moved; the U.S. prosecutors' position (Fortune, 2008) undercuts the Russian characterisation.
